newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian media groups seek deregulation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian media groups seek deregulation.

text.p: Companies involved in Australia's biggest media operations pushed for looser regulation of the industry in their submissions to Canberra's review of ownership rules.
"Cross-ownership restrictions should be removed," News Ltd, the local subsidiary of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, said in its submission.
Technology was blurring divisions in industry, making it counter-productive for a government to try to impose artificial barriers, News said.
News, like most of the other big players who made submissions, commented on foreign investment rules that are not part of the review.
Instead, the government is seeking a discussion paper on only the restrictions on an investor in one type of media sector, such as print, investing in another, such as televisoon.

News said: "Restrictions on foreign investment should be removed. The capital requirements of media industries are substantial: if Australia is to participate in the growth of these industries, and in the jobs they are creating around the world, it must welcome in-bound investment."
Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp has a 57.5 percent economic stake in the Australian Network Ten television group, although its voting power is much less.

"Foreign investment has served to strengthen plurality, diversity and competition in Australia's media industry -- to the definite benefit of the Australian community," Canwest said in its submission.
It accepted that majority ownership and control over Australian media assets should remain in Australian hands for the moment, but a liberalisation of foreign investment rules was still desirable.
"CanWest proposes the following be considered:
"-- Foreign equity interests up to 49.9 percent of voting shares.
"-- No limit on foreign-held non-voting economic interests."
Australian publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd said: "The existing cross-media rules should be phased out and a more flexible system introduced.
"The new system should aim to prohibit acquisitions which would substantially lessen diversity of 'voice'."
"Fixed limits on foreign ownership of the media should be removed immediately.

Applications for foreign investment above 15 percent for individual holdings and 40 percent for all foreign holdings in aggregate should be reviewed by the Treasurer following the policy objectives of plurality, diversity and competition.
Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc, which has a 25 percent interest in Fairfax, said foreign investment should be predictable and the process should be transparent.

"No fixed limits should apply to foreign ownership of Australian media companies and applications should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis in the context of the government's stated objectives," Hollinger said.
The government expects to complete the review within a month or two.
